papers.relied_on: Row 18 cites it (abstract level) for 33 studies, 5362 people and a HOMA-beta correlation of 0.48 with reference methods, as OGTT insulin indices in prediabetes with no treatment use.
papers.full_text_shows: Method validation of surrogate indices against IVGTT or hyperglycaemic clamp; 33 studies after 12,555 titles, 23 low and 10 unclear risk of bias. Highest pooled correlations were for Kadowaki and Stumvoll first-phase indices (30-minute OGTT based); heterogeneity was high (I2 87% for HOMA-beta, 82% for IGI(30)). The pooled 0.48 and the 5362 total are not in the body text supplied (figures or abstract); the prediabetes subgroup HOMA-beta is 0.46 (0.30 to 0.60). It says nothing about treatment decisions.
papers.quote: the most frequently validated surrogate measures are IGI(30) and HOMA-beta
papers.key_numbers: 33 studies; I2 87% HOMA-beta, 82% IGI(30); prediabetes HOMA-beta r 0.46 (0.30-0.60), IGI(30) 0.59 (0.48-0.67); AIR10min vs IGI(30) 0.62 (0.51-0.71)
papers.role_in_work: Supporting citation for row 18 (research endpoint: how well OGTT or fasting indices stand in for first-phase secretion).
papers.design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of correlations (QUADAS-2 inspired bias tool, DerSimonian-Laird random effects)
papers.population_and_size: 33 validation studies in NGT, prediabetes, type 2 diabetes and other groups; 5362 people per row 18 (not confirmed in body text)
papers.measure_type: post-load (OGTT insulin indices) and fasting-based (HOMA-beta) versus IVGTT or hyperglycaemic clamp; C-peptide only mentioned for HOMA2
papers.assay_or_platform: Assays not pooled; same technique used for reference and surrogate within each study; reference methods defined variably (first 3 to 10 min)
papers.quality_note: Few studies per index; high heterogeneity; first phase defined differently across studies; correlation, not clinical accuracy. Authors say OGTT indices also reflect incretin effect and gastric emptying.

papers.relied_on: Row 18: 9,452 people with an OGTT; normal glucose tolerance with 1-h glucose >=8.6 mmol/L resembled isolated IFG with impaired early insulin secretion.
papers.full_text_shows: Single-centre Chinese cohort (Peking University First Hospital) of people referred as at risk. 39.2% of NGT had 1-h glucose >=8.6. Their glucose curve resembled I-IFG, but IGI30 matched I-IGT (11.79 vs 12.04) and exceeded I-IFG (10.93); the oral disposition index was clearly impaired. The disposition-index cut-off (48.5) comes from a reference group of 546 at-risk outpatients, so the 94.6% sensitivity of 1-h glucose is partly circular and the endpoint is an insulin-derived index, not a clinical outcome.
papers.quote: The limitation of this study lies in the selection of the reference group for establishing the norms of the Matsuda Index and DI.
papers.key_numbers: n=9,452; NGT 3,577 of whom 39.2% had 1-h PG >=8.6; Matsuda 3.61 vs 4.64; DI cut-off 48.50; 1-h PG sensitivity 94.6% vs 65.6% (FPG) and 58.0% (2-h); LR- 0.078
papers.role_in_work: Supporting citation for row 18 (OGTT insulin indices in prediabetes; research endpoint).
papers.population_and_size: 9,452 mainly Han Chinese adults at risk of diabetes, 2010-2021
papers.measure_type: post-load (75-g OGTT insulin at 0, 30, 60, 120 min; Matsuda, IGI30, oral disposition index)
papers.assay_or_platform: Roche Cobas e601 electrochemiluminescence immunoassay; intra-assay CV 2.2%, inter-assay CV 2.7%; glucose oxidase
papers.quality_note: Large, one lab, one population; no outcomes; the insulin test is used to validate a glucose threshold, not to guide treatment; reference group not representative.

papers.relied_on: Row 45: postpartum IR cohort; abstract-level association with IR and beta-cell indices, no decision tested.
papers.full_text_shows: Prospective Toronto cohort of 487 women with OGTT in pregnancy and at 3 months postpartum; antepartum adiponectin predicted postpartum Matsuda index (r=0.41), IGI/HOMA-IR (r=0.16) and fasting glucose. Insulin indices are the outcome, not the predictor; the authors suggest adiponectin, not insulin testing, as a risk stratifier. It is longitudinal, not cross-sectional, but measures only metabolic indices 3 months after delivery.
papers.quote: the observational nature of these data cannot conclusively establish causality in the relationship between antepartum adiponectin and postpartum metabolic dysfunction.
papers.key_numbers: n=487 (137 GDM, 91 gestational IGT, 259 NGT); adiponectin vs ISOGTT r=0.41; vs IGI/HOMA-IR r=0.16 (p=0.0009)
papers.population_and_size: 487 pregnant women in Toronto, 3-month postpartum follow-up
papers.measure_type: post-load (OGTT insulin: Matsuda, insulinogenic index) and fasting-based (HOMA-IR)
papers.assay_or_platform: Roche Elecsys 1010 electrochemiluminescence insulin immunoassay, specific insulin (0.05% proinsulin cross-reactivity)
papers.quality_note: Surrogate indices (acknowledged); no diabetes outcome; insulin results used as outcomes.

papers.relied_on: Row 45: mechanistic cohort, no decision tested.
papers.full_text_shows: 166 women with GDM or gestational IGT assessed at 3 and 12 months postpartum; fall in ISSI-2 was linked to worsening hepatic insulin sensitivity (1/HOMA-IR OR 0.13 for declining function; fasting C-peptide:insulin OR 0.95), not to Matsuda or weight. It includes a fasting C-peptide measure (C-peptide:insulin ratio), which the row did not mention. The authors only raise the possibility of an early marker and call for further study.
papers.quote: these data raise the possibility that worsening hepatic insulin resistance may provide an early marker for identifying those women
papers.key_numbers: n=166 (92 decliners, 74 non-decliners); change in 1/HOMA-IR vs change in ISSI-2 r=0.45; OR 0.13 (0.06-0.29); C-peptide:insulin OR 0.95 (0.91-0.98)
papers.role_in_work: Supporting evidence for row 45 (mechanism; also a C-peptide fasting ratio).
papers.design: Longitudinal observational cohort, 3 to 12 months postpartum
papers.population_and_size: 166 women with prior GDM or gestational IGT (Toronto), after excluding those with diabetes
papers.measure_type: fasting-based (HOMA-IR, fasting C-peptide:insulin), post-load (ISSI-2, Matsuda), C-peptide
papers.assay_or_platform: Not stated in the text supplied (described in earlier papers)
papers.quality_note: Indices share glucose and insulin terms with the outcome (ISSI-2), so correlation is partly built in; the change in predictor is measured over the same interval as the outcome.

papers.relied_on: Row 45: cross-sectional cohort; antepartum 2-h glucose OR 2.15 predicted postpartum hyperglycaemia; HOMA-IR not shown to add to glucose.
papers.full_text_shows: Retrospective study of 321 women (28.3% of 1,134) with a single 75-g OGTT at 1 to 6 years postpartum; HOMA-IR was higher in hyperglycaemia than NGT (2.36 vs 1.64), and 2-h glucose in pregnancy (>9.03 mmol/L) was the independent predictor. HOMA-IR was not tested as a predictor of conversion. The authors note insulin is influenced by many factors and suggest C-peptide based HOMA2 might do better.
papers.quote: 75 g OGTT 2 hPG during pregnancy higher than 9.03 mmol/L is regarded as an independent risk factor of postpartum hyperglycemia.
papers.key_numbers: n=321; OR 2.15 (1.245-3.722); HOMA-IR 1.64 NGT vs 2.14 prediabetes vs 4.27 T2DM; 71.7% declined follow-up
papers.role_in_work: Supporting evidence for row 45 (cohort; shows glucose, not insulin, is the predictor).
papers.design: Retrospective cohort with one-time cross-sectional postpartum OGTT
papers.population_and_size: 321 Chinese women with prior GDM (Peking University First Hospital)
papers.measure_type: fasting-based (HOMA-IR, HOMA-beta); glucose OGTT for classification
papers.assay_or_platform: Insulin by chemiluminescence (no platform named); glucose oxidase
papers.quality_note: Selection bias (low attendance), change of GDM criteria, small numbers per year, single visit per woman.

proposals.reason: Row 18 is a research-endpoint row excluded from the scoring candidates (rubric); I found no U or V score for it. The full texts do not change its research-only status.
Full texts confirm association-only cohorts (V21 gave 1, alternative 2). C021 adds a longitudinal link between HOMA-IR change and beta-cell decline, but no diabetes outcome and no decision; keep 1.
proposals.quote: Limitations of this study include the observational design that precludes definitive commentary on causality and the use of surrogate indexes.

proposals.reason: C059 shows 2-h OGTT glucose as the independent predictor and tests no added value of HOMA-IR; no change.
proposals.quote: 75 g OGTT 2 hPG during pregnancy higher than 9.03 mmol/L is regarded as an independent risk factor of postpartum hyperglycemia.

claim_issues.issue: 'resembled isolated impaired fasting glucose with impaired early insulin secretion' holds for the glucose curve only. IGI30 of the 1-h high group equalled I-IGT and was higher than I-IFG; the impairment is in the oral disposition index, whose cut-off (48.5) comes from a reference group of 546 at-risk outpatients. Add: single centre, cross-sectional, no outcomes.

The pooled HOMA-beta correlation 0.48 and the 5362 total are not in the body text I read (figures or abstract only); the text gives prediabetes HOMA-beta 0.46 (0.30-0.60) and I2 87%. Add the heterogeneity caveat and that correlations are with first-phase secretion (IVGTT or clamp), not clinical accuracy.

claim_issues.where: usecases-verified.md row 45 evidence cell ('cross-sectional or mechanistic')
claim_issues.issue: C018 and C021 are prospective longitudinal cohorts (3 months and 3 to 12 months postpartum); only C059 is single-visit cross-sectional. None has a diabetes outcome tested against insulin measures. C021 also used fasting C-peptide:insulin and ISSI-2, not only HOMA-IR and Matsuda.
